definitionEn: the ability of a machine or system to work without wasting energy, time or money
senseNote: Акцент на техническом значении — экономичность машин и систем (fuel efficiency, energy efficiency), а не просто расторопность человека.
situation: Talking about how much useful work a car, heater, factory or office gets from the fuel, time or money it uses.

examples.text: The new engine's [[efficiency]] means the car can travel twice as far on the same amount of fuel.
LED bulbs have a much higher [[efficiency]] than traditional bulbs, which turn most of their power into heat.
By reorganising the warehouse, the company improved its [[efficiency]] and delivered orders a day faster.

texts: Heat pumps work with remarkable [[efficiency]] even in cold weather.
The new manager is obsessed with [[efficiency]] and hates long meetings.
Better insulation is the cheapest way to boost energy [[efficiency]] at home.

badCollocation.noteRu: Помогает ли лекарство или вакцина, описывают словом effectiveness или efficacy. Efficiency — о расходе топлива, энергии, времени.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Экономичный расход топлива — fuel efficiency. Effectiveness и efficacy — о том, работает ли средство вообще, productivity — о выработке.

nuance.text: Engineers measure a heater's [[efficiency]] by comparing the energy it uses with the heat it produces.
nuance.explanationRu: Efficiency — соотношение затраченной энергии и полезного результата. Effectiveness — просто достигается ли цель; для расчёта «энергия на входе — тепло на выходе» нужен efficiency.

reverse.text: Teachers were impressed by the [[effectiveness]] of the new reading programme: pupils' scores rose sharply.
reverse.explanationRu: Программа дала нужный результат — выросли оценки: это effectiveness. Efficiency говорило бы об экономии времени и денег, а не о самом результате.

fixIt.text: Our new washing machine has an excellent energy [[effectiveness]] rating, so it uses very little electricity.
fixIt.explanationRu: Когда речь о расходе электричества или топлива, нужен efficiency: energy efficiency rating. Effectiveness — достигается ли результат вообще.

wordFormation.text: Hybrid cars are popular in cities because of their fuel [[efficiency]] in slow traffic.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Is it worth paying more for a fridge with an A energy rating?"
options: Probably not — its efficiency is so high that it uses twice as much electricity.
Probably, yes. Its energy efficiency is much better, so it'll pay for itself through lower bills.
One must evaluate the efficiency coefficient relative to total lifetime expenditure.
reply.explanationRu: Высокая energy efficiency значит, что холодильник тратит меньше энергии, поэтому верен второй ответ. В первом смысл перевёрнут, третий слишком официален для переписки с другом.

definitionEn: a person's sense of their own importance and value
situation: Talking about how important someone thinks they are and how easily their pride is hurt or flattered.

examples.text: He has such a big [[ego]] that he can't admit he was wrong, even when everyone sees it.
Losing to a complete beginner was a painful blow to the champion's [[ego]].
The project failed because the two directors let their [[egos]] get in the way of sensible decisions.

texts: Winning the award gave her [[ego]] a welcome boost.
Don't take his criticism personally; it's just his [[ego]] talking.
A good leader puts the team before their own [[ego]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Про раздутое самомнение говорят a big, huge или inflated ego. High подходит к self-esteem, а не к ego.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Потешить чьё-то самолюбие — boost someone's ego. Grow и enlarge с ego в этом смысле не сочетаются, а rise — непереходный глагол.

nuance.text: Winning every award has given him an enormous [[ego]]: he now expects everyone to agree with him.
nuance.explanationRu: Ego — самомнение, часто в плохом смысле (a big ego). Self-esteem — здоровая самооценка, и это не порок; про человека, который ждёт всеобщего согласия, говорят ego.

reverse.text: Regular sport can help teenagers with low [[self-esteem]] feel more confident.
reverse.explanationRu: Низкая самооценка — low self-esteem. Low ego так не говорят: ego обычно описывает раздутое самомнение.

fixIt.text: Criticising his work in front of the whole team really hurt his [[self-love]].
fixIt.explanationRu: «Задеть самолюбие» — hurt someone's ego (или pride). Self-love — любовь и забота о себе, а не уязвлённая гордость.

reply.context: Your friend says: "My boss rewrote my whole report and didn't even explain why."
options: That must have boosted your ego — nobody enjoys having their work rewritten.
Your ego has, it would appear, sustained a measurable diminution.
That must have bruised your ego a bit. Maybe ask him what he wanted, so you know next time.
reply.explanationRu: Bruise someone's ego — задеть самолюбие, это и произошло. Boost — наоборот, потешить самолюбие, а второй ответ звучит нелепо официально для разговора с другом.

definitionEn: very detailed and complicated, often planned or made with great care
senseNote: Прилагательное (/ɪˈlæbərət/) — «сложно устроенный, продуманный до мелочей»; не путать с глаголом elaborate (on) — «уточнять».
situation: Describing a plan, design, meal or costume that has many carefully arranged parts and details.

examples.text: They came up with an [[elaborate]] plan to surprise her, involving three cities and a hired violinist.
The dancers wore [[elaborate]] costumes covered in feathers, mirrors and hand-sewn beads.
For their anniversary, she cooked a wonderfully [[elaborate]] dinner with seven courses and a different wine for each dish.

texts: The wedding cake had an [[elaborate]] design of sugar flowers.
Criminals used an [[elaborate]] network of fake companies to hide the money.
The ceremony was long and [[elaborate]], with music and speeches.

badCollocation.noteRu: Трудный экзамен — a difficult или hard exam. Elaborate — не «трудный», а «сложно устроенный, с множеством деталей»: an elaborate plan.

collocationTask.prompt: an ___ plan with fake passports and a secret tunnel
collocationTask.explanationRu: Продуманный до мелочей план — an elaborate plan: это прилагательное. Elaborated — форма глагола, а educated и elevated к плану не подходят.

nuance.text: Guests admired the [[elaborate]] ice sculptures in the hotel lobby.
nuance.explanationRu: Elaborate — искусно сделанный, со множеством деталей, часто вызывает восхищение. Complicated — запутанный, трудный для понимания; для скульптур, которыми любуются, это неудачное слово.

fixIt.text: The thieves had a very [[elaborated]] plan, with fake uniforms and a tunnel under the bank.
fixIt.explanationRu: Прилагательное — elaborate, без -ed: an elaborate plan. Elaborated — форма глагола elaborate (подробно разрабатывать, уточнять).

wordFormation.text: The palace ceilings are [[elaborately]] painted with scenes from ancient myths.

reply.context: A friend asks: "How was your sister's wedding?"
options: Amazing, but very elaborate — three outfit changes, fireworks and a string quartet.
Amazing, but very elaborate — just the two of them and a quick lunch afterwards.
The nuptial proceedings were of a most elaborate nature, one must concede.
reply.explanationRu: Elaborate — пышный, продуманный до мелочей: фейерверк и квартет как раз про это. Скромный обед вдвоём — наоборот, simple, а третий ответ звучит слишком напыщенно.

definitionEn: connected with choosing a government or representatives by voting
situation: Talking about how votes are organised and counted, and how political parties compete to win them.

examples.text: The party suffered a heavy [[electoral]] defeat and lost more than half of its seats.
Critics say the country's [[electoral]] system makes it almost impossible for small parties to win seats.
Independent observers were sent to the region to watch for [[electoral]] fraud during the vote.

texts: Many people are calling for [[electoral]] reform after years of low turnout.
The TV debate could have a real [[electoral]] impact.
Students must register on the [[electoral]] roll before they can vote.

badCollocation.noteRu: Избирательный участок — a polling station. Electoral сочетается с system, reform, campaign, fraud.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Фальсификации на выборах — electoral fraud. Elective — «по выбору, необязательный», electric — электрический, selective — «разборчивый, выборочный».

nuance.text: The government promised [[electoral]] reform so that every vote would count equally.
nuance.explanationRu: Electoral — связанный с выборами: electoral reform, electoral system. Elective — «необязательный, по выбору» (elective surgery, an elective course); к реформе выборов не подходит.

reverse.text: In her final year she took an [[elective]] course in film studies.
reverse.explanationRu: Курс по выбору — an elective course. Electoral относится только к выборам и голосованию.

fixIt.text: Several countries have changed their [[elected]] laws to make voting easier for citizens living abroad.
fixIt.explanationRu: Elected — «избранный» (об избранном человеке: an elected mayor). Законы о выборах — electoral laws.

wordFormation.text: The scandal is unlikely to cause the governing party serious [[electoral]] damage.

rewrite.original: Many young people haven't put their names on the official list of voters.
rewrite.frame: Many young people aren't on the ____.
rewrite.explanationRu: Список избирателей — the electoral roll (или the electoral register).

definitionEn: to raise someone or something to a higher rank, status or level of quality
senseNote: Выбрано значение «поднять на более высокий уровень (должность, статус, качество)», а не просто физически поднять.
situation: When a person gets a more important position, or something is made better, more serious or more respected.

examples.text: After ten years with the firm, she was [[elevated]] to the position of senior partner.
A few fresh herbs can [[elevate]] a simple pasta dish into something special.
The host's thoughtful questions [[elevated]] the debate far above the usual shouting match.

texts: Good lighting can [[elevate]] even a cheap room.
The award helped [[elevate]] the young poet to national fame.
We want to [[elevate]] the level of discussion in our online forum.

badCollocation.noteRu: Цены, зарплаты и налоги повышают глаголами raise или increase. Elevate — о статусе, должности или качестве: elevate the debate.

collocationTask.prompt: to ___ the status of nurses in society
collocationTask.explanationRu: Поднять статус — elevate (или raise) the status. Heighten — усиливать (напряжение, интерес), а grow и enlarge со status не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The new head teacher wants to [[elevate]] the school's reputation as a centre of excellence.
nuance.explanationRu: Elevate — поднять на более высокий уровень статус, репутацию или качество. Increase — увеличить количество (цены, число); increase the reputation звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: The city plans to [[increase]] the number of bike lanes next year.
reverse.explanationRu: Увеличить число чего-то — increase the number. Elevate говорят о статусе и качестве, а не о количестве.

fixIt.text: Thanks to her brilliant results, she was [[lifted]] to the role of head of research last spring.
fixIt.explanationRu: Lift — физически поднимать. Повысить в должности или статусе — elevate (или promote).

wordFormation.text: His sudden [[elevation]] to the board was announced at the annual meeting.
